title: Worker application (client_credentials)
lede: A worker application signs itself in with a client id and secret; the token stays on this app's server. Simulated in Mock.

nodes.label: Your browser
sub: This page. Never sees a token.

nodes.label: This app (server)
sub: Holds secrets and tokens, runs the safety gate, writes the audit.

steps.title: You ask this app
steps.what: You press Test connection or Call. The page asks this app, not PingOne.

steps.title: Worker credentials go to the token endpoint
steps.what: This app sends your worker's client id and secret to the token endpoint (client_credentials).

steps.title: A bearer token comes back
steps.what: A bearer token comes back and stays on this machine's server. The page only learns it is set.

steps.title: The safety gate, then the MCP call
steps.what: The safety gate lets a read through (or checks the confirmation of a write); the app calls the hosted MCP server with the Bearer token.

steps.title: The server acts on the admin API
steps.what: UNVERIFIED that the hosted server accepts a worker token (sources disagree). If it does, the server runs the admin action for the roles the worker holds. A short tool list means missing roles (pingone-mcp skill).
